non_blocking.finding: New in round 4. On the abort path, the runner log loses its abort lines. Line 60 opens the log with '>', which is not append mode, and run_bounded and the sampler inherit that descriptor. abort (line 109) and finish (line 73) reopen the log with '>>', so their lines go to the end of the file, while the inherited descriptor keeps its old offset. When the aborted episode ends, run_bounded prints its record, about 2 KB of JSON (run_bounded.py:63), through the old descriptor. That print overwrites 'SIGTERM received ...' and 'forwarding SIGTERM to the episode's process group ...'. A scratch reproduction of this descriptor pattern kept 0 of the 2 abort lines; with '>>' at line 60, both survive. The dry test missed it because the stand-in prints nothing. The normal path is not affected, and the manifest stays self-consistent. A sampler traceback during finish would clobber lines the same way.

non_blocking.suggestion: Change line 60 to 'exec >> "${P}_runner.log" 2>&1' (the file cannot pre-exist, since the runner refuses if it does). Every inherited copy then appends. Worth doing before the run, because an abort record cannot be redone.

non_blocking.finding: Small edge cases in the abort handler; each window is short or needs an unusual action. (a) Before 'trap abort TERM' (lines 60-131), SIGTERM stops the runner with the default action. Nothing has started by then, so under the rule it is a pre-physics failure, but the note does not say so. (b) For about 0.1 s after the launch, before run_bounded has spawned the episode, 'pgrep -P' finds nothing. The handler then skips the kill and waits for the whole trial, which runs to its end and is labelled 'aborted'. (c) A SIGTERM between the main 'wait' returning and 'LAUNCHER_STATUS=$?' replaces the real status with 1. (d) After the group SIGKILL, the final 'wait "$LAUNCHER"' has no bound if run_bounded itself hangs. (e) 'Send SIGTERM to the runner' must mean its pid, not its process group. A group signal would also kill run_bounded, which has no handler, and the sampler. The handler would then take the still-running episode for finished and remove its container, which is B7's failure mode.
non_blocking.suggestion: Optional hardening: retry pgrep for a few seconds while run_bounded is alive; in the else branch, use 'wait "$LAUNCHER"' when LAUNCHER is set, since bash remembers the status; bound the final wait and SIGKILL run_bounded as a last resort; and write 'the runner's pid (first log line), not its process group' in the note.

non_blocking.finding: Low risk. Lock descriptor 9 is inherited by every process the runner starts, including its own podman calls. If one of them had to recreate podman's rootless pause process, for example after a reboot, that long-lived process would keep the lock, and every later runner would be refused. Today no process holds any v33_trial.lock, and the existing pause process (catatonit, running since 13:25 EDT) holds no lock file.

verified: B7 is closed. A SIGTERM to the runner runs abort(). It finds run_bounded's only child with 'pgrep -P'. That child is the episode leader, which leads its own session and process group; the podman clients and the worker are its children, reached through the group signal and never matched themselves. abort() then signals the group, waits up to 60 s, escalates to SIGKILL, and waits for run_bounded. Finally it takes the normal post-run path, which also stops and removes a container the SIGKILL leaves behind. The header and note now warn against stopping run_bounded alone. In the dry test, the stand-in with run_bounded's process structure recorded exit -15, run_bounded returned within 23 ms, the manifest self-check passed and no episode process was left.

Semantics the coordinator asked about. 'local episode' is assigned before any use, so it is safe under set -u; SAMPLER, LAUNCHER and LAUNCHER_STATUS are set before the trap. 'wait' on a background child that has already been reaped returns bash's remembered status (the dry test got status 1). A SIGTERM during abort or finish is ignored ('trap "" TERM' first). A SIGTERM that lands before finish's first statement is handled by abort, which exits through its own finish, so there is no double finish. Commands started after 'trap ""' inherit the ignored TERM, but the sampler and run_bounded were started earlier and keep their handlers.
